what_failed_live: Two real Room Logins (2026-08-26T22:35:53Z room 11209, 22:37:43Z room 11112, one device 192.168.77.139) VERIFIED and were granted a Purchase, an ACTIVE Entitlement, a device authorization and a Session each. Both then failed at NETWORK ENFORCEMENT: portald abandoned each attempt at its 2500ms budget (scd_unavailable), both Sessions stayed PENDING_ENFORCEMENT, iam_v2 phase3_auth_ipv4 was empty and no tc class existed. Neither guest reached the internet. Root cause: acctd's shaping producer and netd's network writer were both gated on STAYCONNECT_PHASE3_CHECKOUT_GRACE - an unrelated post-departure feature - and netd.env and acctd.env carried no Phase-3 configuration at all.
fix: iamv2.PMSConfig.EnforcementOn(): the enforcement plane follows the Phase-3 MASTER flag, because it is the substrate every guest-session surface stands on rather than a surface of its own. acctd and netd both use it. Checkout Grace was NOT enabled anywhere.

deploy/scripts/check-phase3-enforcement-plane.sh refuses a session-minting surface without a configured plane; install-service-units.sh gates on it as it already gates the Phase-6 guest dependency; a selftest proves the checker refuses the exact live state.

deploy/scripts/enable-phase3-enforcement-plane.sh is the single coherent enabler: it derives the producer uid from the unit acctd actually runs under, writes netd.env and acctd.env, re-runs the checker, and restarts a daemon whose running configuration predates its env file.

internal/enforce: one address is one accountable class, so the newest session owns it and older ones are torn down as SUPERSEDED_ON_ADDRESS. Entitlements are untouched - the uniqueness rules are per subject and a device is not a subject.
cmd/netd: a handover is not a teardown. When the same plan hands an address to a newer session, the kernel state there belongs to its new owner; only the durable half runs for the superseded session.
portald's 2500ms guest budget was REVIEWED against the corrected cycle and left unchanged.

regression_coverage: cmd/netd TestIntegration_EnforcementCycle_* drives the REAL producer (internal/shapeproducer, the call acctd makes) against a real PostgreSQL and submits over a REAL unix socket, so producer authentication is genuine SO_PEERCRED: pending becomes active; an already-pending session is recovered by a restarted applier with an empty state directory; an unauthenticated producer enforces nothing. internal/kerneltest TestKernel_EnforcedGuestIsBothAuthorizedAndAccounted proves on a live kernel that neither half alone grants access, that both together do, that the guest's OWN tc class counts the bytes, and that revoking the gate ends access. cmd/netd TestHandoverLeavesTheNewOwnersKernelStateAlone pins the handover. The measured healthy cycle is 66ms.

pending_sessions_treatment: NOT deleted and NOT rewritten by hand. Both were reconciled by the product's own rules the moment the plane came up: the newest session on the shared address kept it and was enforced; the older one was ended through iam_v2.end_session_enforcement with reason SUPERSEDED_ON_ADDRESS. Neither entitlement was terminated. No Product-Owner policy decision was required, because the question was never which of two entitlements should live - the subject rules already permit both - but which session owns one IP.
defect_found_by_deploying: The first deployment (PR 61) exposed a second defect that only two live sessions on one address and a real second-by-second producer could produce: the superseded session's teardown was removing the surviving session's nft element and tc class, so the guest flickered offline once a second and the accounting origin reset every tick (epoch 3 to 31 in half a minute). PR 62 fixed it; the appliance now shows zero ORIGIN_RESET and a stable generation.
